title: Worker Annotation Persistence Implementation Walkthrough
description: How remote comments were fixed on the Cloudflare Workers deployment.

diagnosis.notes: Console error only. Page bootstraps and comments UI renders.
Caused by shell pattern (server renders loader, client renders artifact). Non-fatal.
Worker had no mutation handler; comments could not be saved.
Worker had no author endpoint; UI fell back to Local Author.

mutations.effect: Adds a new thread with an anchor and initial message
Appends a reply to an existing thread
Updates a message body and timestamps
Removes a message; deletes the thread if it becomes empty
Marks a thread as open again

validation.notes: 24 tests cover parsing, mutation application, and route handling
Created, posted, and deleted a comment on the live artifact

props.content: This walkthrough covers how comments were fixed on the published Cloudflare Worker URL. The fix adds server-side persistence for annotation mutations so remote deployments are no longer read-only.
The user reported comments not working and shared two console errors. Investigation showed the UI actually loaded; the real blocker was missing backend support.

props.caption: Console errors were non-fatal; the 501/404 responses were the real failure.

props.code:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Browser as Visualizer client
    participant Worker as Cloudflare Worker
    participant R2 as R2 Bucket

    Browser->>Worker: POST /api/annotations/proj/slug
    Note over Browser,Worker: Array of mutations (createThread, addMessage, etc.)
    Worker->>R2: GET artifacts/proj/slug/annotations.json
    R2-->>Worker: existing doc or empty
    Worker->>Worker: parse + apply mutations
    Worker->>R2: PUT updated annotations.json
    R2-->>Worker: ok
    Worker-->>Browser: updated annotation document
props.caption: Comment save flow on Workers.dev

worker/test/index.test.ts          # route tests for author + persistence

props.content: Comments now persist on the live Worker. You can open any published artifact, click Comments, select a component, write, and post. The change is committed as `71b37fc` but not pushed.
